errors: No substantive errors. All formulas check symbolically, and the numerical values (8.5, 14.9, 14.5 mm; 29', 20', 34') agree with recomputation from the f.10 data.

Sign convention is not uniform as written. Relative to a direct trace (height, angle) of the two rays, the off-diagonal entries at stations 0 and '' and the diagonal entries α', δ' at station ' are sign-reversed. The determinant αδ-βγ = 1 holds at every station and the final quantities (magnification, eye distance) are right, so this is a convention, not an error.
The label 'Vergrösserung q' on f.10 is a misnomer for the lens separation; the magnification is the row 95.77/91.63/77.46 (= |m|).

The field statement for eyepiece 3 requires '11mm Oeffnung' to be a semi-aperture (radius). The listed eye-lens apertures (3.7, 8, 4.2 mm) would, if they were full clear apertures, vignette eyepieces 1 and 3 more strongly; Gauss evidently treats the field lens as the field stop.

results.what: Paraxial ray transfer through objective plus two-lens eyepiece by two fundamental solutions (axial-parallel ray and chief ray), giving unimodular coefficient pairs at each surface
results.modern_name: Ray-transfer (ABCD) matrix method / Gaussian optics with determinant-1 transfer
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Dioptrische Untersuchungen (1841); matrix formalism later (Sampson 1913 and others)

results.modern_name: Telescope magnification = f_obj/f_eyepiece with two-lens eyepiece focal length bc/(b+c-q)

results.what: Eye distance behind eye lens = c(b-q)/(b+c-q) + a/m^2
results.modern_name: Exit-pupil (Ramsden disc) position / eye relief via Newton's imaging formula
results.usually_credited_to: classical optics (Newton's formula; Ramsden on the exit pupil, 18th c.)

results.what: Field of view = field-stop diameter / distance objective to field lens
results.modern_name: Field of view determined by field stop

results.what: Birth/death/marriage years of Göttingen couples (Hauenschild?, Reinhold, Gräffe)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss's widows' fund work 1845–51 is known

deep.surprise_reason: A competent applied paraxial computation for Gauss's own Repsold instrument. It uses unimodular transfer coefficients that anticipate the formalism of his 1841 Dioptrische Untersuchungen, if the page predates 1841. Gauss's priority claims in dioptrics are already well known, so this is a nice documentary detail rather than a new result.

transcription_corrections: Heading reads 'Distanz des Auges vom 2ten Ocular' (eye distance from the 2nd eyepiece lens = eye lens in light order).
The cancelled expression before the first term is c(q-b)/(q-b-c), equivalent to the retained c(b-q)/(b+c-q).

'zu verlangen[?]' is uncertain; the column values 4.3, 11.4, 9.3 are eye distance minus distance of the eye lens from the front rim (8.5-4.15, 14.9-3.45, 14.5-5.20), i.e. eye position beyond the tube rim. Units are mm, though the page writes '4^m3' or similar.
On f.10 the row labelled 'Vergrösserung q' is actually the lens separation, and the unlabeled row 95.77, 91.63, 77.46 is the magnification m.
'Hauensch.' is probably 'Hauenschild'; 'Heir.' presumably 'Heirat' (marriage); 'Gräffe' likely J. F. C. Gräffe (1754–1816).
